prompt: Three separate square boxes side by side showing how particles are arranged in a solid, in a liquid and in a gas: the first box packed with touching circles in a neat regular grid, the second box with circles touching but jumbled and irregular, the third box with only a few circles far apart and scattered. Draw the circles as plain empty outlines and do not label the boxes. Name the layer groups exactly: solid box, liquid box, gas box, solid particles, liquid particles, gas particles.
subject: chemistry
why: opens every states of matter, kinetic theory or change of state chapter

prompt: Three boxes of particles arranged in a triangle, a solid box of packed circles at the lower left, a liquid box of jumbled circles at the lower right and a gas box of scattered circles at the top, with curved arrows running both ways between solid and liquid, both ways between liquid and gas, and both ways directly between solid and gas. Show arrows only, with no words. Name the layer groups exactly: solid box, liquid box, gas box, melting arrow, freezing arrow, evaporating arrow, condensing arrow, sublimation arrow.
subject: chemistry
why: naming melting, freezing, evaporating, condensing and sublimation in one picture

prompt: A blank pair of axes with a single rising line that climbs steeply, then runs flat, then climbs again, then runs flat a second time, then climbs to the end, giving two horizontal plateaus. Draw the axes as plain lines with short tick marks and put no numbers or words anywhere. Name the layer groups exactly: vertical axis, horizontal axis, solid heating section, melting plateau, liquid heating section, boiling plateau, gas heating section.
subject: chemistry
why: explaining why temperature stays constant while a substance changes state

prompt: Two identical glass gas jars stacked mouth to mouth with a thin glass cover slid between them, the lower jar drawn full of dense stippled dots to show a heavy coloured gas and the upper jar drawn empty, with a second pair beside it where the dots have spread evenly through both jars. Use dots for the gas and add no words. Name the layer groups exactly: lower gas jar, upper gas jar, glass cover plate, dense gas dots, spread out gas dots.
subject: chemistry
why: demonstrating diffusion of a gas and the random motion of particles

prompt: A long horizontal glass tube held level in two clamps on a stand, with a small plug of cotton wool pushed into each end and a narrow ring of white smoke forming inside the tube nearer to the right hand end than the left. Draw the ring as a simple band across the tube and add no words. Name the layer groups exactly: glass tube, left cotton wool plug, right cotton wool plug, white smoke ring, clamp stand.
subject: chemistry
why: linking rate of diffusion to particle mass in the cotton wool tube demonstration

prompt: A beaker of liquid drawn in two stages side by side: on the left a solid lump made of tightly packed circles sits at the bottom surrounded by loose solvent circles, on the right the lump has gone and its circles are spread evenly among the solvent circles. Draw solute circles as plain outlines and solvent circles as smaller outlines, with no words. Name the layer groups exactly: beaker, solute lump, solvent particles, spread out solute particles, liquid level.
subject: chemistry
why: explaining dissolving, solute and solvent at particle level

prompt: A single atom drawn as a small circle at the centre for the nucleus with three evenly spaced concentric circles around it for the electron shells, and small solid dots sitting on the shell circles for electrons. Do not write any numbers or symbols. Name the layer groups exactly: nucleus, first shell, second shell, third shell, electrons.
subject: chemistry
why: the base picture for any atom, electronic structure or bonding lesson

prompt: An atom with one electron shell drawn around it and a magnified circular close up of its nucleus off to one side, the close up packed with two kinds of small circles, one kind drawn with a plus sign inside and the other left plain. Show the plus signs only, with no other letters or numbers. Name the layer groups exactly: atom outline, electron shell, electron, magnified nucleus, proton, neutron.
subject: chemistry
why: distinguishing protons, neutrons and electrons when defining atomic number

prompt: Three atoms in a row, each drawn as a central nucleus circle with concentric shell circles and dots for electrons: the first atom has one filled inner shell, the second has a filled inner shell and a filled second shell, the third has a filled inner shell, a filled second shell and a single dot on a third shell. Do not write any numbers. Name the layer groups exactly: first atom, second atom, third atom, inner shell electrons, second shell electrons, outer shell electron.
subject: chemistry
why: teaching how electrons fill the first three shells

prompt: Three atoms of the same element side by side, each with one electron shell carrying one dot, and each nucleus drawn as a cluster of small circles: the first nucleus holds a single plus marked circle, the second holds a plus marked circle and one plain circle, the third holds a plus marked circle and two plain circles. Add no words or numbers. Name the layer groups exactly: first isotope, second isotope, third isotope, proton, neutron, electron.
subject: chemistry
why: explaining isotopes and relative atomic mass

prompt: A block with a narrow channel holding a small radioactive source aimed at a thin vertical strip of foil, with a curved detector screen wrapped around the foil, and three particle paths drawn as arrows: most passing straight through, one bending as it passes near the foil and one bouncing straight back. Add no words. Name the layer groups exactly: source in lead block, thin gold foil, curved detector screen, straight through path, deflected path, reflected path.
subject: chemistry
why: telling the story of how the nuclear atom replaced the plum pudding model

prompt: A metal atom on the left with a single electron dot on its outer shell, an arrow carrying that dot across to a non metal atom on the right whose outer shell has one gap, and below them the two resulting ions drawn in square brackets with full outer shells. Do not write any charges or letters. Name the layer groups exactly: metal atom, outer electron, transfer arrow, non metal atom, positive ion, negative ion.
subject: chemistry
why: the step between atomic structure and ionic bonding

prompt: Four boxes in a row containing circles: the first holds separate identical plain circles, the second holds pairs of identical circles joined by a short line, the third holds pairs of a large and a small circle joined by a short line, the fourth holds a jumble of single circles, joined pairs and unlike pairs together. Add no words. Name the layer groups exactly: element atoms box, element molecules box, compound molecules box, mixture box.
subject: chemistry
why: sorting elements, compounds and mixtures before writing formulae

prompt: The outline of the periodic table drawn as an empty grid of small blank squares in the correct stepped shape, with the two tall left hand columns, the wide central block, the right hand block and a separate detached pair of rows below. Leave every square completely empty with no symbols or numbers. Name the layer groups exactly: group one column, group two column, central block, right hand block, far right column, detached bottom rows.
subject: chemistry
why: any lesson that points at a position, group or period on the table

prompt: The empty outline grid of the periodic table with a bold stepped staircase line drawn down the right hand side, the large region to the left of the line filled with fine diagonal hatching and the smaller region to the right left plain white. Use hatching rather than solid fill and add no words. Name the layer groups exactly: periodic table outline, staircase line, metals region, non metals region.
subject: chemistry
why: showing where metals and non metals sit and what the staircase line means

prompt: A wide glass trough of water seen from the side with a small piece of metal floating on the surface, a trail of small bubbles rising from underneath it, a ripple where it moves across the water and a small flame above it. Draw the water surface as a single line and add no words. Name the layer groups exactly: glass trough, water, metal piece, gas bubbles, flame.
subject: chemistry
why: the group 1 demonstration in any alkali metals or reactivity chapter

prompt: A wooden test tube rack holding three test tubes of the same size, each about half full of liquid with a clear meniscus line, the liquid in the first tube drawn plain, the second lightly stippled and the third heavily stippled. Add no words or numbers. Name the layer groups exactly: test tube rack, first test tube, second test tube, third test tube, liquid level.
subject: chemistry
why: setting up halogen displacement reactions and their colour changes

prompt: Three atoms side by side drawn as concentric shell circles around a nucleus circle with dots for electrons: the first has one shell holding two dots, the second has an inner shell of two dots and an outer shell of eight dots, the third has an inner shell of two dots and two further shells of eight dots. Every outermost shell is completely full and no numbers are written. Name the layer groups exactly: first atom, second atom, third atom, full outer shells, nucleus.
subject: chemistry
why: explaining why the noble gases are unreactive

prompt: Three atoms in a row growing steadily larger from left to right, each drawn as a small nucleus circle surrounded by concentric shell circles, the first with two shells, the second with three and the third with four, with a long arrow beneath pointing from the smallest to the largest. Add no words. Name the layer groups exactly: smallest atom, middle atom, largest atom, nucleus, electron shells, trend arrow.
subject: chemistry
why: explaining group trends in reactivity from atom size and shielding

prompt: A dot and cross diagram of a metal atom losing its single outer electron to a non metal atom: on the left an atom with shell circles carrying dots, on the right an atom with shell circles carrying crosses and one gap in its outer shell, a curved arrow moving one dot across, and below them the two resulting ions each drawn in square brackets with a full outer shell. Do not write any letters, symbols or charges. Name the layer groups exactly: metal atom, non metal atom, transferred electron, curved arrow, positive ion, negative ion.
subject: chemistry
why: the standard dot and cross picture for any ionic compound

prompt: A giant ionic lattice drawn as a cube of alternating large and small spheres in a regular three dimensional grid, joined by short straight lines, with one small cube of eight spheres pulled slightly out to the side to show the repeating unit. Do not label or write charges. Name the layer groups exactly: lattice cube, large ions, small ions, bonds between ions, repeating unit.
subject: chemistry
why: explaining high melting points and brittleness of ionic compounds

prompt: A dot and cross diagram of two hydrogen atoms bonded together, drawn as two overlapping circles with a shared pair of electrons in the overlap, one shown as a dot and the other as a cross. Do not write any letters. Name the layer groups exactly: first atom circle, second atom circle, overlap region, shared electron pair.
subject: chemistry
why: the simplest covalent bond, taught before water and methane

prompt: A dot and cross diagram of a water molecule: a large central atom circle with two smaller atom circles overlapping it on either side, each overlap holding a shared pair made of one dot and one cross, and two unshared pairs of dots on the far side of the large circle. Do not write any letters or symbols. Name the layer groups exactly: central atom, first outer atom, second outer atom, shared pairs, lone pairs.
subject: chemistry
why: the worked example every covalent bonding lesson draws

prompt: A dot and cross diagram of a methane molecule: a large central atom circle with four small atom circles overlapping it above, below, left and right, each overlap holding a shared pair made of one dot and one cross. Do not write any letters. Name the layer groups exactly: central atom, outer atoms, shared pairs, overlap regions.
subject: chemistry
why: showing four single covalent bonds around one carbon atom

prompt: A dot and cross diagram of a carbon dioxide molecule: one central atom circle with a larger atom circle overlapping it on each side, each overlap holding two shared pairs to show a double bond, and each outer atom carrying two unshared pairs on its far side. Do not write any letters. Name the layer groups exactly: central atom, left outer atom, right outer atom, first double bond, second double bond, lone pairs.
subject: chemistry
why: introducing double bonds after the single bond examples

prompt: A regular grid of identical circles each carrying a plus sign, packed in neat rows, with many tiny loose dots drifting in the spaces between them and a few short motion lines on the loose dots. Show only the plus signs, with no other letters or numbers. Name the layer groups exactly: metal ions, regular rows, delocalised electrons, spaces between ions.
subject: chemistry
why: explaining conduction, malleability and high melting point in metals

prompt: A giant covalent structure drawn as identical circles each joined by four straight lines to four neighbours in a rigid three dimensional tetrahedral network filling the frame. Draw every bond as a plain straight line and add no words. Name the layer groups exactly: carbon atoms, covalent bonds, tetrahedral arrangement, rigid network.
subject: chemistry
why: comparing diamond with graphite for hardness and conductivity

prompt: Three flat sheets stacked one above another with a clear gap between them, each sheet made of joined hexagons of circles, with each circle joined to only three neighbours, short dashed lines drawn in the gaps between the sheets and a few loose dots between the layers. Add no words. Name the layer groups exactly: top layer, middle layer, bottom layer, hexagonal rings, weak forces between layers, delocalised electrons.
subject: chemistry
why: explaining why graphite is slippery and conducts electricity

prompt: A comparison in two halves separated by a vertical line: on the left a few small separate molecules of two joined circles each, floating apart with short dashed lines between them, on the right a single continuous network of circles joined by solid lines filling the whole half. Add no words. Name the layer groups exactly: separate molecules, weak forces between molecules, giant network, strong bonds.
subject: chemistry
why: explaining why some substances melt easily and others do not

prompt: Four ball and stick molecules in a row: a bent three atom molecule, a pyramid shaped four atom molecule, a tetrahedral five atom molecule and a straight line three atom molecule with double sticks between the balls. subject: chemistry
why: moving from flat dot and cross diagrams to real three dimensional shapes

prompt: A Bunsen burner drawn from the side in cross section, showing the heavy round base, the gas hose stub entering the base, the upright barrel, the rotating collar around the bottom of the barrel and the open air hole cut in the barrel behind the collar. subject: chemistry

Add no words. Name the layer groups exactly: closed air hole burner, wavy safety flame, open air hole burner, roaring flame, inner cone.
subject: chemistry
why: teaching the safety flame and the roaring flame

prompt: A filter funnel held in a clamp stand with a cone of folded filter paper inside it, a mixture being poured in from above leaving a layer of solid grains sitting in the paper, and clear liquid dripping from the funnel stem into a beaker below. Do not label the parts. Name the layer groups exactly: filter funnel, folded filter paper, residue, funnel stem, beaker, filtrate.
subject: chemistry
why: separating an insoluble solid from a liquid in any mixtures chapter

prompt: A distillation set up drawn from the side: a round bottomed flask of liquid over a Bunsen burner on a tripod, a thermometer through the bung with its bulb level with the side arm, a sloping condenser with an outer water jacket and two side tubes, and a conical flask collecting drips at the low end. Do not label the parts. Name the layer groups exactly: round bottomed flask, thermometer, condenser, water inlet, water outlet, collecting flask, heat source.
subject: chemistry
why: separating a solvent from a solution and purifying water

prompt: A fractional distillation set up drawn from the side: a flask of liquid on a heat source, a tall vertical column packed with glass beads rising from the flask neck, a thermometer at the top of the column with its bulb at the side arm, a sloping water jacketed condenser and a small receiving flask. Do not label the parts. Name the layer groups exactly: flask, fractionating column, glass beads, thermometer, condenser, receiving flask.
subject: chemistry
why: separating miscible liquids such as ethanol and water

prompt: A beaker with a shallow layer of solvent in the bottom and a rectangular strip of paper hanging into it from a rod across the top, a straight base line drawn across the paper just above the solvent with three small spots on it, and a watch glass resting on the beaker as a lid. Add no words. Name the layer groups exactly: beaker, solvent, paper strip, base line, spots, watch glass lid.
subject: chemistry
why: separating inks and dyes in any mixtures or analysis chapter

prompt: A finished chromatogram drawn as a tall rectangle of paper with a straight base line near the bottom, a straight solvent front line near the top, a single spot part way up, and two vertical measuring arrows beside the paper, a short one from the base line to the spot and a long one from the base line to the solvent front. Add no words or numbers. Name the layer groups exactly: paper, base line, solvent front, spot, distance moved by spot, distance moved by solvent.
subject: chemistry

prompt: A titration set up seen from the side: a long thin burette held upright in a clamp on a heavy stand with a tap near its lower tip, a conical flask of liquid standing directly under the tip and a square white tile under the flask, with a pipette lying on the bench beside the stand. Do not label the parts and write no scale numbers on the burette. Name the layer groups exactly: burette, tap, clamp stand, conical flask, white tile, pipette.
subject: chemistry

prompt: An evaporating basin of solution resting on a wire gauze on a tripod above a Bunsen burner, with wisps of steam rising from the basin, drawn beside a second basin holding a scatter of angular crystals and no liquid. Add no words. Name the layer groups exactly: evaporating basin, solution, wire gauze, tripod, bunsen burner, steam, crystals.
subject: chemistry

prompt: A pear shaped separating funnel held upright in a clamp stand with a stopper in the top, the liquid inside split by a clear horizontal boundary into an upper layer drawn plain and a lower layer drawn stippled, a tap at the bottom of the stem and a beaker underneath. Add no words. Name the layer groups exactly: separating funnel, stopper, upper layer, lower layer, boundary, tap, beaker.
subject: chemistry

prompt: A conical flask with a bung and a bent delivery tube leading into a trough of water, the tube ending under an upturned gas jar that stands on a perforated shelf and is half filled with gas above the water line, with bubbles rising from the tube mouth. Add no words. Name the layer groups exactly: conical flask, bung, delivery tube, trough of water, upturned gas jar, collected gas, bubbles.
subject: chemistry

prompt: A conical flask holding a liquid with a few chips at the bottom, sealed with a bung and a short delivery tube running sideways into the nozzle of a horizontal gas syringe held in a clamp stand, the plunger pushed part way out along the barrel. Do not write any scale numbers. Name the layer groups exactly: conical flask, bung, delivery tube, gas syringe barrel, plunger, clamp stand.
subject: chemistry

prompt: A tall narrow measuring cylinder about two thirds full of liquid drawn large, with unlabelled scale marks up its side, the liquid surface curving down in the middle to form a meniscus, and a simple eye at the side of the cylinder level with the bottom of the curve with a dashed sight line running to it. Write no numbers on the scale. Name the layer groups exactly: measuring cylinder, scale marks, liquid, meniscus, eye, sight line.
subject: chemistry
why: teaching accurate measurement before any quantitative practical

prompt: A three legged laboratory tripod seen from the side with a square wire gauze mat resting flat on its top ring. Draw it plainly with no other apparatus. Name the layer groups exactly: tripod legs, top ring, wire gauze.

prompt: Two identical top pan balances side by side, each with a stoppered conical flask standing on the pan and a blank rectangular display window on the front: the left flask holds a liquid and a separate small solid, the right flask holds the same liquid now fizzing with bubbles. prompt: A test tube held upright in a clamp, about half full of liquid, with a short curled strip of metal near the bottom and a dense stream of small bubbles rising from the strip to the surface. Add no words. Name the layer groups exactly: test tube, acid, metal ribbon, bubbles, clamp.

prompt: A hand holding a burning wooden splint at the open mouth of an upright test tube, the flame just inside the tube mouth and a small burst of short radiating lines drawn at the flame to suggest a pop. Add no words. Name the layer groups exactly: test tube, hand, lit splint, flame, pop burst.
subject: chemistry

Add no words. Name the layer groups exactly: boiling tube, bung, delivery tube, limewater tube, bubbles, cloudy liquid.

prompt: A hand lowering a wooden splint with a glowing tip into the mouth of an upright test tube, the tip bursting into a small flame with short radiating lines around it. Add no words. Name the layer groups exactly: test tube, hand, splint, glowing tip, relit flame.

Add no words. Name the layer groups exactly: first solution, second solution, mixing arrows, third beaker, precipitate cloud, settled solid.
subject: chemistry

Add no words. Name the layer groups exactly: test tube, powder, bunsen burner, bung, delivery tube, limewater tube, bubbles.
subject: chemistry

subject: chemistry

Add no words. Name the layer groups exactly: left beaker, right beaker, tweezers, plain paper strip, hatched paper strip, spare strips.
subject: chemistry

subject: chemistry

Add no words. Name the layer groups exactly: adding excess solid, filtering, evaporating, crystals, arrows.
subject: chemistry

Add no words. Name the layer groups exactly: conical flask, acid, carbonate chips, bubbles, delivery tube, limewater tube.
subject: chemistry

subject: chemistry

prompt: A blank pair of axes carrying three curves that all start at the origin and all flatten out at the same height, one rising very steeply, one less steeply and one slowly, with short tick marks on both axes.
